title: Second-Hand vs New Purchase Ratio
dataSources: Carbon estimates (`carbon:estimate`), recycling weight (`recycling:weight`), food waste (`foodwaste:log`), repairs (`repair:event`).
app: Sustainability telemetry — carbon-footprint apps, home recycling scales, food-waste logs, and repair / reuse journals — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs, MQTT, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=repair:event event=acquisition
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats sum(eval(if(source="secondhand",1,0))) as used, count as total by _time
| eval secondhand_pct=round(100*used/total,1)
| sort - _time
description: Tracks how much of what you buy is second-hand rather than new, a core zero-waste habit.
value: A rising second-hand share cuts waste and cost at once, and seeing it grow reinforces the choice.
implementation: Ingest acquisitions into `index=personal`; compute the second-hand share monthly.
visualization: Column chart of second-hand purchase percentage.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks how much you buy second-hand instead of new, a key part of living with less waste.
